title: Legible: a systemic model of quality and delivery
status: Qualitative causal model; not calibrated or validated as a whole

definition_status.software_quality: The nine elements and meanings supplied by the user on 2026-10-28 are authoritative. Their supplied order defines Q1-Q9 in this revision.
definition_status.systemic: The user supplied the full nine-element systemic-design definition on 2026-10-28: systems thinking plus participatory design, iterative learning and attention to power.
definition_status.validation: Definition alignment is complete. Causal effects remain conditional and not calibrated; stakeholder participation is proposed, not claimed to have occurred.

boundary.unit: One application or service and its contributing value stream; suppliers and shared platforms are explicit dependencies.
boundary.end: Production use, operation and learning that revises intent and implementation
inside: knowledge held only by people, as a source stock; the network and succession stay outside
boundary.purpose: Improve useful and safe outcomes for users while sustaining the ability to change software; a green gate or higher deployment count is not the purpose.
boundary.inventory_scope: All 18 rows in the site's artefact-by-artefact table, using its 2026-10-26 survey as the inventory snapshot. States are site classifications, not an independent fresh audit of every tool.

evidence_legend.M: Measured in a bounded local experiment; its scope and limits travel with the claim.
evidence_legend.R: External primary research supports a related capability or relationship; no claimed tool-specific effect size.
evidence_legend.H: Proposed mechanism or hypothesis in this model; needs local validation.

quality: Performs the required tasks accurately and covers relevant business rules and edge cases.
Independent acceptance outcomes; escaped functional defects; task completion.
Works consistently, handles failures gracefully, and recovers without losing or corrupting data.
SLO attainment, failure injection and verified data recovery.
Is understandable, efficient to use, and accessible to people with different abilities.
Observed task success, user errors and accessibility checks.
Responds quickly and uses computing resources appropriately.
Latency and resource use under a stated workload.
Prevents unauthorized access, protects information, and handles personal data appropriately.
Verified controls, access tests, privacy requirements and exposure.
Is easy to understand, diagnose, fix, and change without introducing defects.
Diagnosis and change effort; change coupling; regression burden.
Allows its behaviour to be verified through effective, repeatable tests.
Repeatable independent tests, controllability and observability.
Integrates with other systems and accommodates changes in platforms, requirements, or workload.
Consumer tests, migration and adaptation scenarios.
Is straightforward to deploy, monitor, support, and troubleshoot in production.
Deployment, monitoring, support and recovery evidence.
quality_notes: The user-supplied nine elements are authoritative; indicators are proposed operationalizations, not extra definitions.
Quality requires measurable, context-dependent acceptance criteria and evidence from users, operators and maintainers.
Artefact quality, product quality, quality in use and delivery performance are distinct but causally connected lenses, not independent silos or four lifecycle stages.
Technical debt is deferred work and future change burden. Safety and compliance remain explicit domain constraints where applicable, without replacing the nine supplied elements.
metrics: DF
Deployment frequency
Production deployments per period; higher capability to deploy is desirable.
Less rework and smaller viable changes can permit more deployments.
Only if demand, deployment automation and release policy allow it; do not manufacture deploys.
CLT
Change lead time
Elapsed time from a code commit to production deployment; lower is desirable.
Fewer downstream corrections and less coordination can shorten the path.
An upstream gate can move work before the commit, or add waiting after it; track both.
CFR
Change fail rate
Fraction of deployments requiring immediate remedial intervention; lower is desirable.
Fewer escaped defects in covered failure classes can reduce failures.
Many defects do not cause immediate deployment failure; denominators and change mix matter.
FDRT
Failed deployment recovery time
Time to recover from a failed deployment needing intervention; lower is desirable.
Current models and trace links can shorten diagnosis and change impact analysis.
Depends on actual responder use, telemetry and recovery controls; fewer failures alone do not shorten this duration.
DRR
Deployment rework rate
Fraction of deployments unplanned because of production incidents; lower is desirable.
Fewer escaped defects can reduce corrective deployments.
Not all rework, debt work or planned improvement qualifies; keep classification consistent.

inventory.tools: pumllint: semantic rules, score, ratchet, trace, editor and CI
inventory.mechanism: Earlier detection of supported modelling defects; author resolves missing decisions before implementation.
inventory.route: CFR/DRR may fall via fewer escaped defects; CLT may fall via less rework; FDRT only if current models aid response.
inventory.limit: A maturity score is not product correctness. Diagram-code drift is not checked by the listed gate. Author-less semantic invention can harm. Drift under a green gate is measured: one maintained set at Level 5, 100/100, with 25 claims the code contradicts (S12 F4).
inventory.evidence: M for a bounded sequence-to-code experiment; H for production effects; M-bounded for drift under a green gate

inventory.tools: aris2puml converts; pumllint checks the resulting activity diagrams
inventory.mechanism: Expose supported process defects to executable checks without silently repairing their source meaning.
inventory.route: Less process misunderstanding may reduce rework and failure; CLT, CFR and DRR are indirect outcomes.
inventory.limit: Conversion fidelity, supported constructs and author review matter. In-ARIS validation still needs an adopter; no automatic transfer of sequence-codegen effect sizes.

inventory.tools: StrictDoc, Doorstop, Sphinx-Needs, OpenFastTrace for structure and links
inventory.mechanism: Find missing or broken references; make requirement ownership and change impact easier to resolve.
inventory.route: Less clarification and omitted impact may improve CLT, CFR and DRR.
inventory.limit: Current structural checks do not establish truth or semantic completeness. The wording linter is planned; ambiguity detection is advisory.

inventory.tools: No maintained checker listed; proposed complement: examples and joint refinement
inventory.mechanism: People expose missing cases and conflicting expectations before code is written.
inventory.route: Avoided misunderstanding may reduce total change time and corrective deployments.
inventory.limit: This is a human-validation intervention, not a shipped machine gate. A story template can be complete while the problem is misunderstood.

inventory.tools: Vale and markdownlint
inventory.mechanism: Consistent terminology and presentation reduce avoidable reading and maintenance friction.
inventory.route: A weak, indirect CLT pathway through comprehension; no direct claim about runtime defect prevention.
inventory.limit: Well-written prose may still contain vague guards or wrong business rules; style cleanup can crowd out substantive review.
inventory.evidence: I + H; R for documentation generally

inventory.tools: gplint; proposed complement: execute independently reviewed examples
inventory.mechanism: Check scenario conventions, then connect useful examples to executable acceptance evidence.
inventory.route: CFR and DRR can improve only through defects actually detected and fixed; CLT through faster diagnosis.
inventory.limit: Linting Gherkin is not running tests. Tests generated from the same mistaken specification can agree with wrong code.
inventory.evidence: I + H; R for test automation generally

inventory.tools: bpmnlint and Camunda plugins; repository-wide extension planned
inventory.mechanism: Detect supported local process-modelling violations before implementation or process execution.
inventory.route: Potentially fewer process defects and less rework: CFR/DRR down and CLT down.
inventory.limit: Do not credit the planned cross-model rules or score today. Local structural validity does not prove business behaviour.

inventory.tools: dmnlint, with the site's stated small rule set
inventory.mechanism: Remove the specific decision-table defects the configured rules detect.
inventory.route: Fewer decision errors may reduce CFR/DRR, if those defects otherwise reach production.
inventory.limit: Do not infer complete overlap, gap, legal or business-rule verification from a lint pass; use independent boundary examples. Measured: 13 tables with 0 gaps, 0 overlaps and 1 untyped output, which was the defect; output typing caught what gap analysis passed (S12 F6).

inventory.tools: pumllint trace today; requirement-model-test-API identifier graph planned
inventory.mechanism: Explicit identifiers expose orphan references and missed change impact across connected artefacts.
inventory.route: Less omitted change scope may improve CLT/CFR/DRR; trace-informed diagnosis may improve FDRT.
inventory.limit: A valid link is not semantic agreement or test adequacy. The full graph and diagram-code drift detection are not shipped by this inventory. Measured: trace reported 158/158 verified while 33 specified statements were never executed; clause-level coverage is the gap. Deleting a requirement's only scenario trips the trace gate; deleting the rule from a requirement that keeps a scenario does not (S12 F6, S13).

inventory.tools: adr-guard and adrpy-ai, both described as pre-1.0
inventory.mechanism: Preserved rationale, ownership and decision status may reduce repeated debate and contradictory changes.
inventory.route: Potential CLT and FDRT improvement through comprehension and diagnosis.
inventory.limit: File validation does not validate a trade-off; stale rationale can entrench a poor design. Keep the site's open classification.

inventory.tools: Structurizr CLI validation and inspections
inventory.mechanism: Make architecture structure easier to inspect and identify supported inconsistencies.
inventory.route: Fewer coordination mistakes may improve CLT; current maps may aid FDRT.
inventory.limit: A valid architecture model does not prove that deployed dependencies match it or that the system meets reliability or performance goals.

inventory.tools: Archi GUI validator and custom scripts, as listed
inventory.mechanism: Human interpretation of validated relationships may improve cross-team change impact decisions.
inventory.route: Potential coordination and CLT benefit, mediated by governance decisions.
inventory.limit: No shared gate-capable catalogue is claimed by the snapshot. Central approval can add more delay than modelling removes.

inventory.tools: Pilot implementation and Capella validation rules
inventory.mechanism: Check supported systems-model constraints and clarify interfaces or stated requirements.
inventory.route: Potential integration-failure reduction; delivery effects depend on system-software interfaces and validation.
inventory.limit: No general standalone gate is credited by the snapshot. Formal model validity is not a safety case; safety requires hazard-specific evidence.

inventory.tools: Spectral, vacuum, Redocly; vacuum score and minimum
inventory.mechanism: Enforce configured contract conventions and make interface expectations explicit before consumer implementation.
inventory.route: Interface defects and rework may fall, improving CFR/DRR/CLT.
inventory.limit: A conforming document is not a verified implementation. Security benefits require relevant rules and tests; backward compatibility is not automatic.

inventory.tools: buf, graphql-eslint, sourcemeta jsonschema; buf breaking checks
inventory.mechanism: Catch supported schema defects and incompatible changes before dependent consumers fail.
inventory.route: A relatively short causal path to fewer integration failures and corrective deployments: CFR/DRR down.
inventory.limit: Schema compatibility does not establish semantic compatibility or safe data migration. Runtime and consumer coverage still matter.

inventory.tools: SQLFluff, dbt-checkpoint, dbt_project_evaluator
inventory.mechanism: Improve supported SQL/project conventions and surface maintainability or structural issues.
inventory.route: Less data-pipeline rework may improve CLT and DRR; some detected defects may affect CFR.
inventory.limit: The site leaves conceptual and logical models uncovered. Lint passes do not prove data correctness, efficient queries or safe migrations.

inventory.tools: pytm and Threagile, with custom risk gating
inventory.mechanism: Make trust boundaries and attack paths discussable; link threats to implemented and verified controls.
inventory.route: Security risk may decrease without any immediate DORA change; CFR/DRR only for affected deployment incidents.
inventory.limit: Generating a threat report is not mitigation. Custom thresholds, control ownership and security testing are required.

inventory.tools: Process-mining conformance, for example PM4Py; custom gate
inventory.mechanism: Compare observed event traces with the model, then investigate deviations and revise design or execution.
inventory.route: Reduced recurrent process defects and bottlenecks may improve end-to-end time, CFR and DRR.
inventory.limit: Requires suitable logs and case identities. Deviations can be beneficial adaptations; conformance to a bad process is not quality.

inventory.tools: No gate in the inventory; the experiment's glossary check (terms used repeatedly and defined nowhere) is a candidate
inventory.mechanism: A defined term is one identity across artefacts; an undefined recurring term is a decision nobody wrote.
inventory.route: Fewer silent disagreements between artefacts may reduce rework and omitted change scope: CLT and CFR, indirect.
inventory.limit: Measured once: 42 of 60 recurring kit terms had no definition before wave 2 (S12 F8). A definition is not agreement on meaning.
inventory.evidence: I + H; M-bounded for the gap

inventory.tools: Covered by a practice: hypothesis-style property tests on the specified invariants, run against the original and each rebuild
inventory.mechanism: Properties exercise behaviour no example scenario reaches, independently of the examples the kit states.
inventory.route: Detection of behaviour the scenario suite misses: CFR and DRR, indirect.
inventory.limit: Measured once: six intrinsic properties at 100 examples each and one differential property, 7/7, on one program (S12). A property holds for the cases generated, not for all.
inventory.evidence: M-bounded on one program; H elsewhere

actors: Users and domain owners
Validate intent, edge cases and acceptable outcomes
Can reject a semantically wrong 'green' artefact; supply independent examples.
Product owners and sponsors
Choose scope, priorities and improvement capacity
Do not convert freed capacity automatically into more unfinished work.
Analysts and architects
Own models, interfaces, rationale and dependencies
Maintain source truth; distinguish unsupported constructs and missing decisions.
Developers and AI agents
Consume artefacts and implement changes
Resolve uncertainty with an owner; agents cannot authorize invented business meaning.
QA, security and safety specialists
Choose independent acceptance and risk evidence
Challenge shared assumptions; gate on justified risk, not document appearance.
Platform and gate maintainers
Own check precision, latency, versions and integration
Tune rules, make failures actionable, audit suppressions and baseline changes.
Operations and responders
Use current context and report production behaviour
Feed incident causes and observed drift back to authors; verify recovery paths.
Governance and risk owners
Set proportional controls and exceptions
Time-bound waivers with accountable ownership; change incentives when scores are gamed.
practices: P1
Run at the author and in CI
Shorter feedback delay and less avoidable handoff work
Measure time-to-action and usefulness, not tool-install count; S1/S6.
P2
Separate clean / findings / unable-to-run
Makes the check result actionable and its failure visible
An unexecuted check must not silently become a pass; S1.
P3
Use severity and a justified threshold
Focus scarce review effort on consequential defects
Do not hard-block low-precision ambiguity judgements; validate rule precision locally; S1.
P4
Baseline and ratchet
Allows brownfield adoption while exposing regression
Baseline update outside the gate; new/untracked work needs an explicit policy. A ratchet alone does not repay old debt; S1/S3.
P5
Use stable IDs and machine-readable reports
Makes change-impact links and review evidence retrievable
Record what inputs, versions and scope were checked; a link or report is not a semantic proof; S1.
P6
Tag evidence and publish failures
Limits false confidence and supports revision of rules
Keep local experiment results separate from external research and untested mechanisms; S1/S3.
P7
Validate intent with people and independent tests
Prevents common-mode errors across requirements, models, tests and code
Site-level complement to the inventory: stakeholders, walking skeleton and shipped-product feedback; S1/S10.
P8
Review incidents and observed deviations
Closes the loop from actual outcomes to upstream intent
Proposed implementation practice; distinguish useful exceptions from defects and update artefacts deliberately; H.
P9
Calibrate the oracle by mutation
Tests the tests before any rebuild, so detection is independent rather than shared-premise
Planted mutants must fail the suite; m1 failed 2 scenarios and m2 failed 11 before any recreation ran (M-bounded, S12 F7).
Elicit what only people know
Fills upstream omissions at their source and shrinks the assumption stock
Inventory from traces before any session; worked cases, counterexamples, exception walks, incident replay, quirk and orphan adjudication, with the successor present (H, S14).
Externalise into the normative home, with a check
Turns an elicited item into shared, current knowledge that drift can be measured against
Rules to decision tables, terms to the glossary, flows to models, reasons to decision records, procedures to runbooks; the register links provenance and is never a second source of truth (H, S14).
Validate every extracted claim with its owner
The independent channel that breaks the reverse path from code into derived artefacts (E73)
Observed, inferred and intended kept apart; a defect preserved for compatibility is a recorded decision with scope and an example; feeds E57 (H as a practice; the channel is M-bounded, S12 F2).

nodes.label: Unresolved upstream artefact defects

nodes.label: Defects in behaviour-carrying derived artefacts
nodes.definition: Wrong assumptions embodied in contracts, decision tables, data definitions and executable examples: the artefacts a builder takes behaviour from

nodes.label: Implementation defects

nodes.label: Inherited test-oracle errors

nodes.label: Effective independent detection
nodes.definition: Detection based on relevant evidence that does not merely repeat the disputed assumption

nodes.label: Dependent artefact reach
nodes.definition: Number of relevant downstream consumers and dependencies for an upstream decision

nodes.label: Affected downstream items
nodes.definition: Distinct artefacts, components or services carrying consequences of an upstream defect

nodes.label: Defect detection latency
nodes.definition: Time between introduction and reliable detection of a defect

nodes.label: Correction scope
nodes.definition: Artefacts, components, data and stakeholders requiring coordinated correction

nodes.label: Operational exposure
nodes.definition: Relevant users, transactions or operations exposed to faulty behaviour over time

nodes.label: Adverse outcomes in use
nodes.definition: Observed errors, disruption, loss or other user/operational consequences

nodes.label: Knowledge held only by people
nodes.definition: Intent, rules, exceptions and history that no artefact in the inventory states; held by people, in the strong sense (cannot be fully told) or the weak sense (sayable, unwritten). The network and succession are outside the model.

nodes.label: Platform and dependency change
nodes.definition: A change in a platform, library or runtime that alters behaviour the code assumed, downstream of any intent

nodes.label: Defects in explanatory artefacts
nodes.definition: Wrong assumptions embodied in models and prose that explain structure or intent without carrying executable behaviour

nodes.label: Diverse independent derivation
nodes.definition: Independent re-derivations of the same artefact from the same inputs, whose divergences are triaged rather than scored away

nodes.label: Completeness against an inventory
nodes.definition: Coverage of a requirement inventory by a derived artefact, measured separately from the precision of what it states

edges.condition: Test derivation repeats the faulty premise without an independent oracle

edges.mechanism: Shared faulty expectations can hide implementation errors despite passing tests.
edges.condition: The affected requirement is not independently challenged elsewhere

edges.mechanism: Detection followed by containment or valid correction prevents relevant faults escaping.
edges.condition: Findings are acted on and regression checks cover the correction

edges.mechanism: Implementation defects can escape into production when relevant checks miss them.
edges.condition: Comparable detection and deployment scope

edges.mechanism: Domain-author validation resolves wrong or missing intent before it is reused.
edges.condition: Validation has sufficient domain knowledge and independent evidence

edges.mechanism: Independent examples and reality checks can expose a common wrong premise.
edges.condition: Other relevant factors held comparable

edges.mechanism: Validated correction removes defects from the relevant upstream scope.
edges.condition: One code-only revision of the kit took spec defects from 2 to 0 and non-identical artefacts from 22 to 11, all 11 by construction (S12 F7)

edges.mechanism: Additional relevant upstream defects may affect more dependent items.
edges.condition: Comparable dependency structure; count unique impacts without treating every copy as a new root cause

edges.mechanism: One wrong decision can affect several dependent artefacts or components.
edges.condition: The dependency actually carries that decision; simple link count is insufficient

edges.mechanism: More affected items can require a wider coordinated repair.
edges.condition: Other relevant factors held comparable

edges.mechanism: Late detection can leave more dependencies, persisted data and commitments to unwind.
edges.condition: Consequences accumulate; delay does not inevitably increase scope

edges.mechanism: Wider coordinated correction can consume more unplanned effort.
edges.condition: Comparable repair automation, reversibility and component isolation

edges.mechanism: Escaped defects can impair outcomes experienced by users or operators.
edges.condition: The faulty behaviour is exercised and relevant consequences are not contained

edges.mechanism: More use of faulty behaviour can spread its consequences.
edges.condition: Comparable defect severity, containment and user context

edges.mechanism: Observed adverse outcomes can prompt investigation and validated learning.
edges.condition: Outcomes are observable, attributed and acted upon; learning is not automatic

edges.mechanism: Correcting source intent and dependent artefacts can remove the originating defect.
edges.condition: Root cause is addressed; a local workaround alone does not resolve upstream intent

edges.mechanism: Pressure can encourage unresolved assumptions and rushed source changes.
edges.condition: Ownership, time and incentives permit incomplete or guessed intent to be handed on

edges.mechanism: Passing checks based on the wrong premise can postpone reliable detection.
edges.condition: Other relevant factors held comparable

edges.mechanism: Independent domain examples can correct faulty expected outcomes or omitted cases in tests.
edges.condition: The independent evidence is valid and the test oracle is actually updated

edges.mechanism: What only a person knows is omitted from the written intent: the author did not know, or knew and did not write.
edges.condition: The person is not in the authoring loop, or the item is tacit in the strong sense

edges.mechanism: What was never written arrives at the builder as an assumption; a kit stands in for a person it cannot ask.
edges.condition: Assumption-register entries per artefact set are the measured shadow of this stock: 65, 50 and 30 from a code-derived kit, 117 and 94 from a generated wiki (S12 F5)

edges.mechanism: Derivation treats implemented behaviour, defects included, as intent.
edges.condition: The derived artefact is calibrated to the implementation, not to independent intent: the timestamp unit and the export crash both reached code-derived artefacts (S12 F1)

edges.mechanism: A changed platform or dependency alters behaviour the code assumed.
edges.condition: No test pins the assumed behaviour: pandas 3.0.5 turned a millisecond stamp into seconds (S12 F1)

edges.mechanism: Unresolved intent is copied into models and prose as readily as into contracts.
edges.condition: The disputed intent is consumed and not corrected

edges.mechanism: An explanatory artefact carries behaviour only when it is the builder's sole behavioural input; otherwise its defects are attenuated by the behaviour-carrying layer.
edges.condition: Attenuation measured: 12 diagram defects reached no rebuild, and defects planted only in diagrams reached nothing, because a higher-ranked layer stated the behaviour (S12 F3, S13 D1)

edges.mechanism: A passing structural gate over a drifted artefact reads as assurance.
edges.condition: The gate scores the set against itself, never against the code: a Level 5, 100/100 set carried 25 claims the code contradicts (S12 F4)

edges.mechanism: Independent derivations disagree where a shared premise is wrong; the disagreement is the detection.
edges.condition: Divergences are triaged, not scored away: two rebuilders refused cleanly where the original crashes, and both recorded it (S12 F2)

edges.mechanism: Coverage of an inventory finds the omissions that precision cannot see.
edges.condition: Accurate but incomplete is the measured shape: claim precision 0.992 against strict coverage 0.245 (S12 F5)

loops.title: Prevention and reinvestment
loops.reading: Better effective checking can reduce reactive work and release capacity for more prevention. It can also run in reverse.
loops.leverage: Protect some freed capacity for authorship, rule tuning and debt reduction.
loops.evidence: H as a whole; E03 has bounded experiment and related research support

loops.title: Firefighting and bypass
loops.reading: Escapes consume time, pressure rises, checks are bypassed and the defect-prevention system deteriorates.
loops.leverage: Limit WIP and protect time to resolve findings; reward surfaced uncertainty.

loops.title: Approval and batching trap
loops.reading: Responding to failure with more burdensome approval can create larger batches and further failure.
loops.leverage: Use fast, risk-sensitive checks and peer decisions close to the work; monitor queues.
loops.evidence: R-related capability evidence; H for a particular local implementation

loops.title: Green but wrong
loops.reading: Score-oriented semantic invention can produce apparent success, reduce independent challenge and perpetuate unresolved intent.
loops.leverage: Escalate missing intent to its owner; require independent outcome examples, not just a higher score.
loops.evidence: M for E27 and bounded repair; M-bounded for drift feeding confidence (E77); H for the organizational loop

loops.title: Corrective risk control
loops.reading: Relevant controls can counter deployment failures, provided they improve effective checking instead of merely adding burden.
loops.leverage: Compare B1 against competing R3; calibrate precision and response, not strictness alone.

loops.title: Reality-based learning
loops.reading: Observation exposes mismatch, and owned learning reduces it by changing the model or the implementation.
loops.leverage: Maintain useful runtime evidence and independent review; conformance is not automatically the right objective.
loops.evidence: H; one instance M-bounded: a model set read against its code, adjudicated, spot-checked by execution (S12 F4)

loops.title: Cascade and rushed repair
loops.reading: Unresolved intent propagates into implementation; escaped defects generate reactive work and pressure, which can encourage further unresolved intent.
loops.leverage: Resolve the root assumption and all affected dependants; protect time for validation rather than just patching symptoms.
loops.evidence: H as a loop; the model-to-code leg has bounded M support

loops.title: Outcome-led source correction
loops.reading: Observed harm can drive validated learning that corrects the originating intent and interrupts recurrence.
loops.leverage: Use independent user and operational evidence, accountable source owners and impact-aware correction.
loops.evidence: H; depends on observation, attribution and action

Unresolved upstream defects
Count within an explicit artefact scope
introduced by new or changed intent; removed by validated correction
A warning count is an observation, not the stock itself.
T
Technical and information debt
Estimated remediation effort, hours
deferred work and drift add effort; verified remediation removes it
Estimates require re-estimation; not interchangeable with defect count.
K
Validated, current shared knowledge
Count of owned, validated knowledge items
validation adds; invalidation and stale context remove
Coverage, relevance and use matter more than volume.
W
Work in progress and waiting
Changes in a consistently defined workflow
admitted changes add; completed or abandoned changes remove
A larger W stock can increase waiting even if coding is faster.
N
Unresolved or invented decisions
Assumption-register entries per artefact set
unstated intent adds; validation and externalisation remove
Measured on five rebuilds: 65, 50, 30 from a code-derived kit; 117, 94 from a generated wiki. A count of assumptions, not of defects.
P
Knowledge held only by people
Items in a capture inventory: found, validated, externalised with a check, residual by name
elicitation and externalisation remove; departures and unrecorded decisions add
No percentage of knowledge captured: the population has no denominator. Its downstream shadow is N.
hypotheses: H1
Precise early checks prevent relevant escaped defects
Run an applicable high-precision rule subset; record confirmed findings, corrections and targeted escape classes.
Confirmed early catches rise initially; targeted escapes and unplanned correction work fall later.
If escapes do not change despite genuine coverage and consumption, inspect rule relevance, propagation and test blind spots.
H2
Gate burden can outweigh prevention
Track wait and triage time by stage; introduce advisory-first checks and compare similar change cohorts.
False positives or centralized sign-off increase waiting and bypass before any delayed quality gain.
If burden is material without prevented defect evidence, tune, relocate or remove the gate instead of escalating strictness.
H3
Traceability reduces omitted change impact
For changes with known dependent consumers, compare identified impacts with independently reviewed actual impacts.
Fewer missed consumers and shorter diagnosis after the trace is used.

If links exist but are stale or unused, graph coverage is not a leading indicator of the claimed benefit. Measured once: trace reported 158/158 requirements verified while 33 specified statements were never executed (S12 F6).
H4
Intent validation prevents 'green but wrong' repairs
Flag guessed or unresolved decisions; require domain-owner resolution and independent outcome examples.
Incorrect repairs decline even if gate scores change little.

If no independent oracle exists, do not infer correctness from matching specifications and tests. Measured once: a kit derived from code wrote the original's crash into the spec as a requirement, the rebuild reproduced it, and the suite scored it as correct (S12 F2).
assumptions: Edge polarity means same-direction (+) or opposite-direction (-) change, holding stated conditions comparable; it does not mean good/bad or a numerical coefficient.
Delay categories are modelling assumptions, not estimated effect timings.
A directed path to DORA is a testable causal hypothesis, not proof that buying or installing a named tool changes that metric.
Checks influence only represented properties within their supported scope; unknown and unrepresented requirements remain outside the gate.
Automation and human practice are complements; reported findings must be interpreted and resolved with valid intent.
Local linter, score and documentation improvements cannot by themselves establish deployed runtime quality.
systemic_elements: Treat upstream-to-downstream defect propagation as a candidate explanation; revisit boundary and assumptions.
Involve authors, domain owners, users, implementers, testers and responders; their costs and priorities differ.
Show dependency branches, shared assumptions, feedback, power, incentives and delays across the four quality lenses.
Investigate why invalid assumptions survive, why tests share them and why pressure displaces correction.
Agree useful, dependable outcomes and acceptable trade-offs, beyond green gates and deployment counts.
Resolve intent early, diversify validation evidence, reveal change impact and protect correction capacity.
Combine relevant checks with domain clarification, independent acceptance, traceability and runtime feedback.
Observe propagation, escapes, exposure and rework; revise the model when evidence contradicts it.
Assign owners, fund maintenance and learning, and govern exceptions and obsolete assumptions.

cascade.interpretation: The four layers are distinct analytical lenses with causal links; they do not form a mandatory linear or waterfall process.
mechanisms: Wrong or missing meaning is inherited by a downstream decision or implementation.
One root defect reaches several artefacts, components or teams through relevant dependencies.
Tests, code and models share a faulty premise, so agreement and green checks can delay discovery.
Further decisions, integration, persisted data and commitments expand the correction scope.
Use turns latent faults into consequences for users, operations and the business.
Implemented behaviour, defects included, is read back into artefacts derived from the code; an oracle calibrated on the same code passes the inheritance as correct.
What propagates is decided by the highest-ranked layer that states the behaviour; a defect in a lower layer loses to a correct higher one, and a wrong value in the highest wins.
limits: Propagation is conditional, not inevitable. Independent validation, domain expertise, containment and supported checks can stop or attenuate it.
A defect need not become semantically more wrong at every stage. Its spread, exposure, correction scope or consequences can grow while the root error remains the same.
Some downstream faults are introduced independently and cannot be attributed to upstream artefacts.
No universal late-fix cost multiplier or monotonic quality decline is asserted.
The full cascade and its DORA effects are hypotheses, not a measured production outcome of the tool inventory.
Attenuation holds only while a higher-ranked layer still states the behaviour correctly; a defect planted consistently in every layer propagates and is concealed by the derived suite.
measurements: Root defect ID, originating artefact/version and independent basis for calling it wrong.
Downstream items actually affected, confirmed by impact analysis rather than link count alone.
Where inherited errors were detected, corrected, contained or escaped; detection delay.
Shared assumptions between code, tests and reviews; independently verified missed cases.
Correction scope, rework effort, exposure and observed user/operational impact, separately from root-defect count.
Assumption-register entries per artefact set, as the count of what the inputs did not state.
Per planted or found defect: propagated, attenuated, or recorded as an assumption; and which gate, if any, saw it.

revision_notes: v0.2 makes cross-layer propagation, branching into tests, amplification mechanisms and containment explicit in the visualization.
The nine quality elements now follow the user-supplied definition; Q-code meanings differ from v0.1, and inventory mappings were reconciled.

v0.3 applies the out-of-sample review (S12, F1-F7) and the degradation test (S13, D1-D2): a reverse edge from code into derived artefacts, a dependency-change source, derived artefacts split by role with precedence as the moderator, drift feeding confidence, an indicator for the unknown stock, diverse derivation and completeness as detection inputs, oracle calibration as a practice; and one extension, a source stock for knowledge held only by people with two edges and three practices, all H until the departing-expert pilot runs. Two inventory rows added (A19, A20). No magnitudes; no edge from capture to delivery metrics.
